rows.notes: v1 had under_construction, 50 GWh {phase1:20, phase2:30}. Now: Jiemian (2026-03-19) says EVE has 'built and put into production 9GWh' in the Chengdu zone => operational (partial), installed 9 GWh, installed basis: press. Nameplate: the 2022 plan was 50 GWh in two phases (CNY 20bn) but only the dated part is kept per conventions: built 9 + 21 GWh 46-series large-cylindrical project (company convertible-bond roadshow, 2025-03-22; construction period 3 years) = 30 GWh. Ref year 2027 = the company-revised 'ready for use' date of that 21 GWh project (2027-12-31, announcement 2025-12-31); this is a project completion date, not an explicit 达产 statement. Undated remainder of the original 50 GWh plan (~20 GWh) is in notes only. The 9 GWh line vs the 21 GWh 46-series project are treated as different capacity. v1 start_year 2022 was the announcement year, nulled (no source for first production year). Chemistry/format/end_market nulled: only the planned 21 GWh is stated as NMC 46-series cylindrical; existing 9 GWh line technology not found. Separate solid-state pilot base (100 MWh) in Chengdu is not this row.

Huizhou (Zhongkai) is EVE's home base and a multi-plant hub; the annual report lists Huizhou first among its domestic production bases, so operational. No source gives a site-level GWh/yr figure for the existing Huizhou plants, so nameplate/installed are null (company-wide 2025 shipments 50.15 GWh power + 71.05 GWh storage are not site capacity). Chemistry/format/end-market nulled (mixed prismatic LFP/NMC, cylindrical, sodium - not site-sourced). Separate NEW project, 60 GWh Tonghu/Zhongkai, announced 2026-03-27, added as its own row (not merged here). Sodium-ion HQ (2 GWh, groundbreaking 2025) added as its own row. Hub nameplate stays null so nothing is double counted.

Hub of 18 factories (EVE's largest base). Local press (2025-07-30) says capacity grew from 3 GWh to 169 GWh across 18 factories; used as installed (basis: local-government/press, 13-year cumulative). v1 used 152.61 GWh from Wikipedia (early-2023 target) - replaced. NAMEPLATE is a floor: 169 does not include the 60 GWh 'super factory' phase 2 (construction began Jan 2025, 'under construction' per the same article; total plan 60 GWh, CNY 10.8bn) beyond whatever of phase 1 is already in the 169, and excludes a separate new 60 GWh Jingmen project announced 2026-03-31 (CNY 6bn, 亿纬动力; announcement only, not added as a row because the hub row represents the site). Whether the 169 includes the ~15-17 GWh phase 1 of the super factory is not stated. ref year 2025 = publication year of the figure (no 达产 statement found). Chemistry/format/end-market 'mixed' (LFP large prismatic Mr.Big storage cells, cylindrical, NMC) - not individually quoted. Dug for a cleaner current figure with a Chinese-language search; none found. No ESCALATE: confidence 0.65.

The 2025 annual report names a Ningbo subsidiary (宁波亿纬创能锂电池有限公司, 'Ningbo Chuangneng') in its environmental-disclosure list and lists Zhejiang among the domestic production bases, so a producing Zhejiang plant exists; the report does not state that it makes cells, nor any capacity. Searches in Chinese and English found no Ningbo-specific capacity, chemistry or date. All numeric fields null. Status 'operational' is inferred from the annual report listing Zhejiang as a production base (low confidence 0.4; capacity unknown so not a large-plant gate issue).

EVE-Linyang JV (EVE 65% / Linyang 35%, Yicai 2021-06-11; ~CNY 3bn, plan 10 GWh per the same article and v1). I could not open a page confirming the 10 GWh capacity, the 2022-11-18 first-line start, chemistry or format (the v1 source 91jinshu returned 503; asianmetal returned an error page), so those are nulled rather than carried. Status operational is inferred from the annual report listing Jiangsu as a production base (weak: not Qidong-specific) plus the 2022 first-line report seen only as a search snippet. NEW: 2026-04-07 company announcement of a separate 50 GWh storage (power) battery base in Qidong Economic Development Zone (CNY 5bn, 332 mu, needs shareholder vote) - announcement only; recorded in operator_sites, not added as a row (same city/zone as this site). Per-site nameplate left null: if the lead wants 10 GWh back, a quote from Linyang Energy's 2022 announcement is needed.

Operational: EVE research-institute head (2025-04-01) says the Qujing LFP large-cylindrical line is 'already in mass production'. Nameplate 23 GWh/yr (CNY 5.47bn, 3-year build) per the 2025-03-22 convertible-bond roadshow; ref year 2025 = publication year of the figure (the same source gives only a 3-year construction period, no calendar 达产 year - searched, none found). RISK: the 2025 annual report (A4) says the 23GWh project's construction content and total investment were changed in Aug/Sep 2025 and renamed '磷酸铁锂储能动力电池项目'; the new capacity is not given in any open page I could open, so 23 GWh may be stale. Installed capacity not sourced (null). v1 start_year 2024 and 'mixed' details not confirmed -> start_year null. Chemistry LFP and cylindrical from Q1/Q2; end-market 'mixed' from 'power-storage' (动力储能) wording. Qujing is also named a national zero-carbon park base in the annual report (A3).

Company announcement (2022-09-27): Shenyang plan 40 GWh storage+power batteries, CNY 10bn, two phases (phase 1 CNY 5bn / 20 GWh). Base opened 2025-06-30: 'Pilot Project' (大圆柱 for BMW) trial production + systems factory in formal production; Solarbe says this marks the base 'formally starting production operations' => operational, start_year 2025. capacity_ref_year 2022 is the fallback (publication year of the nameplate source; I searched for a 达产 year and found none) - treat the year as unknown. v1 capacity_by_year {2025:10} dropped (no source for 10 GWh cylindrical phase). Installed capacity not stated in any open page -> null. Cell format cylindrical (大圆柱); chemistry null (46-series NMC for BMW not quoted for this site); end-market mixed (EV cylindrical + storage/systems). A 2022 announcement listed 'two' BMW large-cylindrical plants: Shenyang and Debrecen. 21 GWh 46-series project in the 2025 convertible bond is in Chengdu, not Shenyang.
Wuhan R&D branch / energy-storage institute lab only (business scope: research and development). Cell manufacturing in Hubei is at Jingmen (kept as hub row).

Phase 1 started production Feb 2025 (battery-news.de): 680 million 21700 cylindrical cells/yr, converted by the article to 'just over ten' GWh (installed basis: press conversion). Phase 2 plant building was completed Feb 2026 (just-auto, 2026-02-25: '684 million prismatic and cylindrical cells per year across 15 lines' - cell count, no GWh); the annual report (A2) confirms the Malaysia base is built. Nameplate 10 GWh is therefore a FLOOR (phase 1 only); phase 2 and the separate storage-battery expansion (company 2025-06 announcement, max CNY 8.654bn, ~38-48 GWh cumulative per press snippets I could not open) are unquantified here. v1 values 20 GWh {2025:10, 2026:20} not source-confirmed -> replaced. ref year 2025 = publication year (fallback). Not a JV (v1 JV note about Invest Kedah removed: state agency only). Chemistry null (21700 cells; NMC/LFP not stated).

Yuxi 10 GWh project (agreement 2022-05-17, CNY 3bn; MarkLines 2022-07-05 says construction began) now at the planning-permit publicity stage (ITDCW, 2026-04-16), which implies no real construction yet. Status kept at 'announced' (the 2022 'groundbreaking' was ceremonial and the permit is only now being approved) - alternative: under_construction on the strength of the 2022 MarkLines item; rejected. Per-project state 'active' (no source says paused), but no progress news 2022-2026 except the permit notice -> flagged ESCALATE. ref year 2026 = fallback publication year; no target year found.

Hithium Chongqing Southwest Intelligent Manufacturing Center, Tongliang district (not Chongqing city centre; v1 coordinates are a city centroid - left unchanged). Design 56 GWh cells + 22 GWh modules, CNY 13bn. Phase 1 (28 GWh) started Dec 2023 (press release 2023-12-13 'will release 28 GWh ... successively'); phase 2 'fully in production in September (2026)' per Sina (2026-09-30) => installed 56 GWh as of 2026-09-30, basis: company design capacity (not effective output). Ref year 2026 from that phase-2 statement. Plant ran at full load since March 2025 (Yicai 2025-09-25). v1 had no values (web was blocked). Xiamen v1 56 GWh was this plant's figure - corrected on the Xiamen row. start_year null (no quote with the year 2023 captured); chemistry/format null (not quoted). Press 'cumulative shipment 200 GWh' event 2026-10-15 held here.

Heze long-duration storage integrated zero-carbon park: construction started Oct 2024, mass-production roll-off Aug 2026 (Sina 2026-09-30; 10jqka 2026-08-09 'phases 1 and 2 fully in operation'; STDaily 2026-08-07). Full-output design: 30 GWh cells (1175Ah LDES cells) + 20 GWh systems, CNY 13bn. Only the 30 GWh cell figure is used (20 GWh is system assembly). Installed capacity at Aug 2026 not stated -> null. ref year 2026 = publication-year fallback; no explicit 达产 year found. Large single lines (>15 GWh/line). Chemistry/format not quoted -> null.

Announced only (investment agreement signed 2026-04-15/16 in Beijing, ~EUR 400-405m; site not final - Esquiroz/Galar former BSH plant is one option). Navarra councillor (press, not opened) quoted 7.5 GW for cell production - a GW figure, not GWh/yr, so nameplate stays null. Production 'could' start 2027 (planned; start_year 2027 is plan, not actual). v1 coordinates (42.8169, -1.6432) are the Pamplona area, not a confirmed site - left unchanged, treat as approximate. Phase arithmetic: phase 1 (M1 smart factory, 5 lines) 15 GWh/yr (started 2022-05-29) + phase 2 30 GWh/yr (8 lines, groundbreaking 2022-06-01, planned complete 2023) = 45 GWh/yr. Hithium's own plants page: 'The entire project was completed in 2023'. Yicai (2025-09-25): Xiamen and Chongqing at full load since March 2025. Installed 45 GWh = design capacity basis (company/press), as of the Yicai date. v1 56 GWh was the CHONGQING design figure - removed. A secondary article (The Paper, 2025-04-08) says Xiamen 'planned annual capacity 450 GWh'; this is almost certainly a typo for 45 (Hithium shipped 35 GWh in 2024) and is not used. ref year 2023 from the company statement. start_year null (the 2022 reports quote no year in the text). LFP from H5. Xiamen coordinates are city-level (Torch Hi-tech Zone) - unchanged.

Discovery candidate (T026). EVE's first European cell plant, next to BMW's Debrecen plant: construction began Nov 2023 (electrive.net 2023-11-30, then planned 28 GWh, start 2026); 2025 annual report: project 'progressing smoothly'; July 2026 reporting: first-phase 30 GWh/yr, production scheduled 2027 (slipped from 2026; second half of 2027 per a Jan 2026 report not opened). Nameplate 30 = first phase (the only dated figure); ref year 2027 = scheduled start of production, not a 达产 year. 46-series large cylindrical (大圆柱) for BMW Neue Klasse; chemistry not quoted. Operator entity name from the annual report glossary (EVE Power Hungary Kft.). Coordinates omitted (not found at site level).

rows.notes: Discovery candidate (T026). CORRECTION to the candidate row: the plant is in Byhalia (Marshall County), Mississippi, not Lexington - both FleetOwner and electrive say Byhalia. JV of Accelera (Cummins), Daimler Truck and Paccar at 30% each with EVE Energy as technology partner (10%, electrive 2025-10-22). Groundbreaking mid-2024. Delays: Paccar said production would not start until 2028 (Oct 2025); by May-July 2026 'that timeline has been shelved, no new target has been set'; structure to be finished by end-2026 but equipment not installed (FleetOwner; Transport Topics 2026-07-15; Daimler Truck took a EUR 200m impairment). => project_state paused (indefinite delay, building shell still being completed). Capacity 21 GWh/yr LFP (electrive 2025-10-22), ref year 2025 = publication-year fallback (no target year exists). Operator listed as Amplify since EVE is a 10% partner, not the operator. The FleetOwner article's date (2026-06) is the month the 'shelved' wording was published (search listing); the FleetOwner page itself did not show a date, so published is approximate.
